results.contract: Cached bootstrap skips dotenv; configuration is the stable application access boundary.

optionReview.rationale: The configuration file captures the environment value when the cache is built, and the service reads that stored configuration.
Moving execution to boot does not change cached bootstrap: .env still is not loaded.
Refreshing the cache does not make subsequent cached bootstrap load .env for a service-level env call.
A true fallback masks a missing value and ignores an intended false deployment setting.

results.contract: Retry and refresh are separate maintenance response headers.

optionReview.rationale: Refresh controls a Refresh header for browser reload behavior, not Retry-After.
Status selects the HTTP status code; 45 is not the required 503 or a retry delay.
The retry option supplies Retry-After on the maintenance response.
Redirect changes where clients are sent rather than providing the requested 503 retry hint.

results.contract: The standard application builder passes bootstrap/providers.php into provider registration.

optionReview.rationale: Middleware aliases identify request middleware; they do not register service providers.
A route file does not treat its returned value as a provider list.
Autoloadability permits loading a class but does not request provider registration.
The application bootstrap reads that provider list and registers its entries.

results.contract: Provider boot is a distinct phase after eager registration, and boot supports container injection.

optionReview.rationale: Laravel registers the eager providers before booting them, so B has supplied its binding when A boots.
Construction occurs before registration completes and makes the timing problem earlier.
Both access the same container at the same premature lifecycle stage.
Singleton lifetime does not make B's not-yet-registered binding available.

results.contract: Scoped registration combines singleton resolution with lifecycle-specific instance flushing.

optionReview.rationale: A singleton can retain mutable state for the worker lifetime, crossing the job boundary.
An explicit instance is shared without the requested scoped lifecycle reset.
Scoped services share one instance in a lifecycle and are flushed before the worker begins the next lifecycle.
A transient binding creates different objects on repeated resolutions within the same job.

results.contract: The deferred manifest maps provided abstracts to provider classes.

optionReview.rationale: The manifest uses service identifiers, not source-file paths.
Laravel maps each advertised service abstract to its deferred provider and loads that provider when the abstract is resolved.
Configuration dependencies do not identify the service being resolved from the container.
Consumers are not the abstract keys used to trigger deferred service loading.

lint.wrapper: PHP opening tag; scope supplied in question metadata

results.contract: Terminate resolves a middleware instance separately; sharing handle state requires an appropriate lifetime or external request-local state.

optionReview.rationale: The termination phase calls the container to make the middleware, so state from handle is not guaranteed on that new object.
next has no generic property-reset mechanism; a different resolved instance explains the observation.
Termination is a later phase; the issue is object identity, not reversed lifecycle order.
The standard kernel does not serialize these middleware objects for termination.

results.contract: Trusted-host middleware establishes allowed host patterns; URL escaping and APP_URL address different concerns.

optionReview.rationale: Host validation rejects unapproved hostnames before application code relies on them for absolute links.
HTML escaping prevents markup interpretation but does not make a destination hostname trusted.
Proxy trust determines which forwarded data is used; it does not provide the required host allowlist.
APP_URL is not a general incoming Host allowlist for HTTP requests.

results.contract: The middleware builder stores custom aliases for the HTTP kernel/router alias table.

optionReview.rationale: Appending makes it global and does not supply the required paid alias mapping.
That file registers service providers, not route middleware aliases.
The alias map resolves the short route middleware name to the class without adding it globally.
A route name is unrelated to resolving middleware("paid").

results.contract: The kernel global pipeline precedes router dispatch; route exclusions operate later on a separate list.

optionReview.rationale: Route naming has no such interaction with middleware exclusions.
Provider registration does not determine whether route middleware exclusions apply.
Exclusions operate on middleware entries, not on selected sections of their handle methods.
The global pipeline is assembled separately from the route middleware list where exclusions are applied.

results.contract: Legacy instance middleware discovery resolves the controller while gathering route middleware; static HasMiddleware follows a different path.

optionReview.rationale: A route name does not supply the tenant state required by the business operation.
Even the first route middleware has not run when early controller middleware discovery constructs the controller.
A singleton does not make the first construction later and risks retaining another request's tenant.
The controller can be instantiated to discover its instance middleware before that route pipeline executes; the action runs after middleware setup.

results.contract: On mutex contention, the command returns a numeric isolated option value or its configured default isolation exit code.

optionReview.rationale: The default contention exit is success unless configured otherwise, so this does not express the required 12.
Quiet mode changes console output, not the exit code used when the isolation lock is unavailable.
A numeric value supplied to isolated is used as the exit code when the isolation mutex cannot be acquired.
Disabling interaction prevents prompts; it does not select the contention exit status.
